diagnosis: High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion with mixed basaloid and warty-type features
legend: The epithelium is thickened and replaced by small atypical cells with hyperchromatic nuclei and scant cytoplasm. There is no prominent pleomorphism. There is architectural disorganization with a wind-blown appearance in the lower two thirds of the epithelium. Superficial parakeratosis is present. Abundant melanophages are visible in the papillary dermis.

diagnosis: High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion of the vulva
legend: Strong and diffuse block-type staining with p16. There is both cytoplasmic and nuclear positivity. The staining is particularly useful to rule out HPV-independent differentiated intraepithelial neoplasia with unusual basaloid or warty-like features. p16 is typically overexpressed in high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions.

diagnosis: High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion of the vulva
legend: With mixed basaloid and differentiated features. The lesion shows prominent hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, and anastomosis of the interpapillary ridges. The lower thirds of the epidermis are disorganized and replaced by the immature hyperchromatic cells with high N:C ratios. Some mitotic figures are easily identified. The epithelium seems to mature superficially. In some areas, atypia appears to be limited to the basal layer.

diagnosis: High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion of the vulva
legend: Basaloid type. The epidermis is fully replaced by small atypical hyperchromatic cells with large nuclei, scant cytoplasm, and prominent mitotic activity.

diagnosis: High-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion of the vulva
legend: Warty type. The epidermis has a warty architecture, with deep and wide rete ridges. There are koilocytic-like changes.

diagnosis: High-grade squamous intraepitelial lesion (HSIL) of the vulva
